newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurer PZU Life sees '96 net doubling.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurer PZU Life sees '96 net doubling.

text.p: Polish insurance company Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen na Zycie SA (PZU Life) sees its net profit doubling in 1996 from last year's 58 million zlotys, the company said in a statement.
It did not give any details of the forecast.
In the first three quarters of 1996 the company reported a net profit of 58.2 million zlotys, down from last year's 81.6 million.

It said the lower profit in the January-September period resulted from a change in the company's investment portfolio, now made of instruments with maturities longer than one year, revenue from which is not shown in quarterly earnings reports.
Pre-tax profit in the first nine months of 1996 slipped to 66.8 million zlotys from 117.9 million zlotys last year.

Gross premiums in the three quarters rose to 1.6 billion zlotys from 1.2 billion a year ago while revenue from investments rose to 326.4 million zlotys against 266 million in the same period last year.
PZU Life, a subsidary of state-owned PZU SA giant has an 87.3-percent share of the life insurance market in Poland.
